text:
Emma: heads-up — I put together a small proposal to tighten up the status headers and client-facing copy for routing/quota signals. want quick feedback before I open a PR :eyes:
Raj: dropping in. is the primary goal less noisy logs or clearer SDK surface?
Emma: both. current problem: we emit very verbose human strings in headers (e.g. `X-Rdwd-Route-Reason: fallback_due_to_capacity_region_us-east-1_pool_small`) which bloats logs and complicates SDK parsing. idea: switch to short canonical tokens + a mapping table in the console/docs.
Sylvia: agree with canonical tokens. but SDKs parse headers today for retry/backoff logic. we need stable tokens and semantic versioning for mappings (so older SDKs keep behavior).
Will: from console side — mapping table is fine but we also need plain-language banner copy for customers. they shouldn't see `route:cap_burst` anywhere; show `Performance reduced` or `Limited capacity` with a tooltip that expands to the mapping.
Emma: exactly. proposal sketch:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Rdwd-Status-Token: ROUTE_CAPACITY
X-Rdwd-Status-Sub: REGION_BURST
X-Rdwd-Telemetry-Tag: route_reason=CAPACITY;quota_bucket=burst;mapping_v=2023-11

// SDKs should treat ROUTE_CAPACITY as a retryable class w/ client hint in payload.
```
Raj: +1 for compact token names. question: do we keep 3xx/4xx split semantics? e.g., should we ever return 503 for capacity vs 429?
Sylvia: semantics matter. 429 is rate/quota-like; 503 is service-level degrade. we should codify a matrix: token class -> canonical HTTP status. that matrix lives in docs and the console mapping.
Maya: ops angle — when we change tokens, can we emit an audit event to `infra.events` so SRE dashboards can filter by token instead of free-text? ops-bot could auto-create an incident when TOKEN=ROUTE_CAPACITY and freq>threshold.
ops-bot: noted. I can add a daily aggregation for `X-Rdwd-Status-Token` and emit alerts when count > 5000 in 5m. confirm config?
Will: for customer UX: short banner copy + a console link to "Why this happened" (pre-populated query on token). example copy: "Performance reduced — temporary capacity constraints. See details." tooltip: "ROUTE_CAPACITY: traffic rerouted to a lower-throughput pool"
Emma: also thinking about rollout:
- phase 0: add headers in shadow mode (emit token headers but don't rely on them)
- phase 1: SDKs consume tokens for client-retry hints (opt-in flag)
- phase 2: console mapping published; banner copy uses mapping_v to pick language
- phase 3: deprecate old verbose header fields after 90 days

Sylvia: additive ask: include `mapping_v` in telemetry so we can run backfills and map old logs during transition. also provide a stable set of token docs (and a no-break policy for token strings).
Raj: can we get a sample of the console mapping JSON? I want to validate SDK logic against it.
Emma: sample mapping: 
```json
{
  "mapping_v": "2023-11",
  "tokens": {
    "ROUTE_CAPACITY": {"http_status": 429, "class": "retryable", "console_message": "Performance reduced"},
    "QUOTA_EXHAUSTED": {"http_status": 429, "class": "terminal", "console_message": "Quota exceeded"},
    "SERVICE_OVERLOAD": {"http_status": 503, "class": "degraded", "console_message": "Service degraded"}
  }
}
```
Sylvia: good. SDKs need `class` mapping too. terminal vs retryable affects backoff strategy. keep it simple: `retryable | terminal | degraded`.
Maya: ops-bot, please add `mapping_v` to logs and hook to the alert rules. ops-bot: will do, creating a PR for aggregation config.
ops-bot: created infra/alerts/agg-token-counts PR #42 (link: https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/42) :thumbsup:
Will: copy/UI nit — console should show the human phrase and an expand to the canonical token and a small timestamp when the mapping was last updated. add a little note: "If you rely on header tokens in production, pin `mapping_v` in your client config."
Emma: last thing: i18n. console copy needs translations. `console_message` can be a key; the UI will render localized strings. I'll add an internationalization column to the mapping doc.
Raj: sounds solid. next steps: Emma opens PR with header names, the mapping schema, and the rollout timeline. I'll review SDK impact and write a short migration guide.
Sylvia: I'll own the token stability policy and the compatibility windows.
Will: I'll mock the banner + tooltip and post screenshot tomorrow.
Emma: thanks all — i'll open the PR and tag @Raj @Sylvia @Will. posting doc draft: https://redwood.dev/routing-status-proposal (WIP).
Raj: thanks — :thumbsup:
